entities.summary: La Palma’s Ruta de los Volcanes in Spain is a demanding ridge traverse through pine forest, craters, volcanic ash and lava with ocean views.
entities.description: Follow the marked GR 131 south from Refugio El Pilar to Los Canarios on La Palma for changing volcanic terrain and Atlantic views on both sides in clear weather. Repeated climbs and a long loose descent make this roughly 5.5-hour outing demanding. Arrange a taxi or transfer to the start; there is no normal direct public bus. Carry ample water, as none is dependable after departure. Check live weather and trail notices: declared adverse-weather alerts close La Palma’s trails. The lighthouse extension is separate.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Ruta de los Volcanes on La Palma sustains volcanic variety across a full mountain walk, linking craters, pine woods and open ocean-facing ridges.

variants.name: Ruta de los Volcanes — El Pilar to Los Canarios
variants.description: Follow the marked GR 131 from Refugio El Pilar along La Palma’s Cumbre Vieja volcanic ridge to Los Canarios. The walk passes pine forest, craters and loose volcanic slopes; the separate continuation to Fuencaliente lighthouse is excluded.
variants.accessNotes: This is a point-to-point route. Leave transport at Los Canarios and arrange a taxi or supported transfer to Refugio El Pilar; there is no normal direct public bus to the trailhead. The final approach into Los Canarios includes a brief surfaced village-road finish, so use sidewalks where present and stay alert to traffic.
variants.seasonalLimitations: The official network currently lists the route open, but all La Palma trails close automatically during declared adverse-weather alerts. Avoid the hottest summer days and check the live Cabildo trail status and weather immediately before departure.
suitabilityConstraints: Requires strong endurance for repeated climbing, a long loose descent and roughly five and a half hours of exposed mountain walking.
Unsuitable in severe wind, extreme heat, wildfire restrictions or poor visibility; there is no dependable water after the start.
warnings: Carry ample water, food, sun protection, wind and rain layers, mountain footwear and offline navigation backup.
Loose lapilli and volcanic rock make the long descent tiring and can be slippery; cloud and wind can remove the defining views and increase navigation risk.
Expect a brief surfaced village-road finish in Los Canarios; use sidewalks where present and stay alert to traffic.
Stay on the signed GR 131 and obey current protected-area, wildfire, volcanic-area and adverse-weather closures.
The Good Shit line is descriptive and non-navigation-grade; current signs, closures, weather and Cabildo instructions take precedence.

entities.summary: Reserva Ibèrica’s Rambla shop in Barcelona specialises in Iberian cured ham, with a tasting counter for comparing pieces before buying.
entities.description: At Reserva Ibèrica on Rambla de Catalunya in Barcelona, taste Iberian cured ham and ask staff how origin and curing change the pieces. The business selects fully Iberian-breed pigs at source and supervises curing, making comparison more useful than buying an anonymous plate. Ask about acorn-fed ham and try the tasting section before choosing takeaway slices or a larger piece. Premium whole hams are expensive; check current tasting prices and reserve any specific cutting or pairing activity.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Reserva Ibèrica in Barcelona lets visitors learn differences in Iberian cured ham through comparative tasting and staff guidance before buying.
